updates.name: Ed Buskey
updates.bio: Professor of Marine Science at the University of Texas at Austin, working in Port Aransas, and research coordinator for the Mission-Aransas National Estuarine Research Reserve from 2006 to 2023. Studies zooplankton behavior and sensory ecology, plankton bioluminescence, predator-prey interactions, harmful algal blooms, and the effects of crude oil and dispersants on plankton.
updates.research_interests: plankton biology; coastal ecosystem processes; marine ecosystem dynamics; marine population dynamics
updates.current_affiliation: The University of Texas at Austin, Department of Marine Science (Marine Science Institute, Port Aransas)
updates.notes: Identity: archived MarineGEO Gulf Coast Texas page (web.archive.org 20250329074510, re-fetched 2026-10-26) links 'Ed Buskey' to the old utmsi.utexas.edu Buskey profile; the current UT Marine Science directory page is headed Edward Buskey. ORCID 0000-0002-1729-6640 (Edward Buskey) has no employment on record, so it is not recorded. No Google Scholar link on the profile. Status not stated (Professor, 1999-present).

updates.name: Ed Proffitt
updates.bio: Professor of Biology in Life Sciences at Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi whose marine ecology research covers plants and invertebrates of marshes, mangroves, oyster reefs and seagrass beds. Teaches experimental design and biostatistics, and has held posts at universities, federal agencies, consulting firms and local government. Holds a PhD in biology from the University of South Florida.
updates.research_interests: marsh ecology; mangrove ecology; oyster ecology; seagrass ecology; invertebrate ecology
updates.current_affiliation: Texas A&M University-Corpus Christi, College of Science - Life Sciences
updates.notes: Identity: the archived MarineGEO Gulf Coast Texas page (web.archive.org 20250329074510, re-fetched 2026-10-26) links the name 'Ed Proffitt' to this exact TAMU-CC profile, which is headed 'Charles Proffitt'. updates.name: Simon Brandl
updates.bio: Heads the Brandl Lab (Fish & Functions) at the University of Texas at Austin's Marine Science Institute in Port Aransas, Texas. The lab examines the ecology, evolution and functional roles of coastal fishes, from organismal biology and community assembly to each species' part in ecosystem fluxes of energy and nutrients.
updates.research_interests: biodiversity; coastal ecosystem processes; nutrient cycling
updates.current_affiliation: The University of Texas at Austin, Department of Marine Science (Marine Science Institute, Port Aransas)
updates.notes: Identity: archived MarineGEO Gulf Coast Texas page (web.archive.org 20250329074510, re-fetched 2026-10-26) links 'Simon Brandl' to the old utmsi.utexas.edu profile; the UT Marine Science directory profile (200) gives title and fields of interest and links the lab site fishandfunctions.com, whose footer links scholar.google.ca/citations?user=nTZjpZcAAAAJ. updates.name: Barbara J. Bond
updates.bio: Emeritus professor in the Department of Forest Ecosystems & Society at Oregon State University. A forest ecologist studying physiological processes, chiefly water and carbon relations, of trees and whole forest ecosystems, and developing tools to measure and monitor them. Holds a B.S. from UC Irvine and M.S. and Ph.D. degrees from Oregon State.
updates.research_interests: forest ecology; tree and forest ecosystem physiology; water and carbon relations; tools for measuring and monitoring forest physiological processes
updates.current_affiliation: Oregon State University, Forest Ecosystems & Society
updates.notes: OSU College of Forestry directory entry (node/7750 redirects to /people/bond-barbara, 200), titled Emeritus Professor, Forest Ecosystems & Society; Andrews Forest is an OSU site. No ORCID or Scholar link on the page; no ORCID recorded.

updates.name: Frederick J. Swanson
updates.bio: Research geologist and emeritus scientist with the USDA Forest Service Pacific Northwest Research Station in Corvallis, retired since 2012 yet still doing some research. Investigated the physical processes shaping forests and streams, much of it at the H.J. Andrews Experimental Forest. Courtesy professor in Oregon State University's Forest Ecosystems and Society department; honored by AAAS.
updates.research_interests: aquatic ecosystems; disturbance ecology; erosion and other disturbances in forest and mountain stream environments
updates.current_title: Emeritus scientist, USDA Forest Service PNW Research Station; Emeritus Faculty, OSU Forest Ecosystems & Society
updates.current_affiliation: USDA Forest Service Pacific Northwest Research Station; Oregon State University

updates.name: Jerry F. Franklin
updates.bio: Professor emeritus in the University of Washington School of Environmental and Forest Sciences, a forest ecologist called the father of 'new forestry'. Expertise covers forest and landscape ecology, disturbance, old-growth and forest management, including harvest strategies that weigh ecological with economic values. Among the first scientists at Mount St. Helens after its 1980 eruption.
updates.research_interests: forest ecology; landscape ecology; disturbances; old-growth forests; forest management
updates.current_affiliation: University of Washington, School of Environmental and Forest Sciences
updates.notes: Existing homepage https://environment.uw.edu/faculty/jerry-franklin/ returned 404; replaced by the UW News expert profile (200). Personal page https://faculty.washington.edu/jff/ also returns 200 but shows an old College of Forest Resources title. ORCID search found 0000-0002-8211-6247 (Jerry Franklin) with no institution, so not recorded. No Scholar link found.

updates.bio: Ecologist with the USDA Forest Service Pacific Southwest Research Station, now listed by the agency as a former employee. Holds a doctorate in forest science from Northern Arizona University (2002), a public policy master's from Harvard's Kennedy School and a B.A. from William & Mary; the profile's publications address wildfire, tribal ecocultural restoration and forest management.

updates.name: Mark D. Schulze
updates.bio: Director of the H.J. Andrews Experimental Forest and senior research assistant professor in Forest Ecosystems & Society at Oregon State University. Interests include tropical forest ecology and management, how forest ecosystems and species respond to climate variability and disturbance, and phenology and trophic interactions. PhD from Pennsylvania State University (2003), then a postdoc at the University of Florida.
updates.research_interests: forest ecology; tropical forest ecology and management; forest ecosystem and species responses to climate variability and disturbance; phenology and trophic interactions

updates.name: Sherri L. Johnson
updates.bio: Holds a courtesy appointment in Oregon State University's Department of Fisheries, Wildlife, and Conservation Sciences, working in aquatic ecology and biogeochemistry. Studies how landscapes shape streams: stream-forest interactions, how hydrology, temperature and geomorphology affect stream organisms and ecosystem functions, and network and patch dynamics. PhD in zoology, University of Oklahoma (1995).
updates.research_interests: aquatic ecology; biogeochemistry; stream-forest interactions; hydrology, temperature and geomorphology effects on stream biota; network and patch dynamics
updates.current_affiliation: Oregon State University, Department of Fisheries, Wildlife, and Conservation Sciences

updates.name: Mark E. Harmon
updates.bio: Professor emeritus in Forest Ecosystems & Society at Oregon State University, working in forest, wildlife and landscape ecology. Research topics include ecosystem succession, decomposition, nutrient cycling, carbon dynamics and landscape dynamics. Trained at Amherst College (B.S.), the University of Tennessee, Knoxville (M.S.) and Oregon State (Ph.D., 1986).
updates.research_interests: forest ecology; ecosystem succession; decomposition; nutrient cycling; carbon dynamics; landscape dynamics
updates.current_affiliation: Oregon State University, Forest Ecosystems & Society
